editorial.summary: The finale confirms Alaska and David's claimed completion of all fifty states. After a private-plane ride, the crew marks property, enters a hotel room by invitation and joins Mark, Cornelius and unnamed people for an improvised haircut/bleaching scene whose hospitality, religious talk, explicit objects and dreams remain distinct from later doubts and apparently left-behind property. Daniel recommends leaving Anchorage for the countryside and points them toward North Pole. The crew then hides in a minivan on a car carrier, stages dangerous climbing/fishing stunts, tries to feed a moose and shelters in an unknown structure near Fairbanks while David speaks for the entire crew's health. A giant Spider-Man-style hand earns a ride from Ralph, whose explicit refusal of camera is followed by David's unsupported felon joke. Santa and Mrs. Claus are performance roles, not legal identities. David's brief moral uplift collapses into another argument with Harry before the final apology and recap. All ideas remain literal; corrections, safety, privacy, rights and identity provenance remain separate.
